title: Constraining Primordial Power Asymmetry from Galaxy Clustering and Peculiar Velocity Information
summary: Primordial power asymmetry would probe departures from statistical isotropy, offering a clue to the physics of the primordial Universe. We investigate how such asymmetries can be tested with galaxy surveys and quantify how peculiar-velocity information can improve these tests. We develop a unified bipolar spherical harmonic (BipoSH) analysis of the auto- and cross-power spectra of galaxy density and line-of-sight peculiar velocity, and perform Fisher forecasts combining a Euclid-like spectroscopic galaxy survey with peculiar velocities reconstructed from Simons Observatory-like CMB maps through the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect. For dipolar asymmetry, we consider both scale-independent and scale-dependent modulations proportional to $k^{-0.5}$. Galaxy clustering provides most of the constraining power in both cases, while peculiar velocities add only modest information. For quadrupolar asymmetry, we account for the recently identified anisotropic galaxy-bias response and marginalize over its amplitude. We find that galaxy clustering alone suffers from a degeneracy between the primordial quadrupolar modulation and anisotropic galaxy bias. This degeneracy can be substantially broken by adding peculiar-velocity information: the density-velocity cross-spectrum provides complementary information to the galaxy auto-spectrum, while the velocity auto-spectrum constrains the primordial modulation independently of anisotropic galaxy bias. The velocity information becomes increasingly effective for more negative scale dependence, yielding constraints tighter than those from BOSS for scale dependences proportional to $k^{-1}$ and $k^{-2}$. Our results demonstrate that peculiar-velocity information provides a complementary avenue for testing primordial power asymmetry with large-scale structure, particularly for quadrupolar asymmetry in the presence of anisotropic galaxy bias.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how primordial power asymmetries can be tested using galaxy surveys combined with peculiar-velocity information (reconstructed from CMB via kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect). Using a unified BipoSH framework for auto- and cross-power spectra of galaxy density and peculiar velocity, the authors find that while galaxy clustering dominates constraints on dipolar asymmetry, peculiar velocities are crucial for quadrupolar asymmetry—breaking degeneracies with anisotropic galaxy bias and providing scale-dependent constraints tighter than BOSS for steep scale dependences.
AI.motivation: Primordial power asymmetry would reveal departures from statistical isotropy, providing clues about the physics of the early Universe. The authors aim to quantify whether and how peculiar-velocity information can improve tests of such asymmetries with upcoming galaxy surveys combined with CMB-derived velocity reconstructions.
AI.method: The authors develop a unified bipolar spherical harmonic (BipoSH) analysis of auto- and cross-power spectra of galaxy density and line-of-sight peculiar velocity. They perform Fisher forecasts combining a Euclid-like spectroscopic galaxy survey with peculiar velocities reconstructed from Simons Observatory-like CMB maps via the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect, considering both scale-independent and scale-dependent dipolar modulations (k^{-0.5}) and quadrupolar asymmetry with anisotropic galaxy-bias response marginalized over.
AI.result: For dipolar asymmetry, galaxy clustering provides most of the constraining power; peculiar velocities add only modest information. For quadrupolar asymmetry, galaxy clustering alone suffers from a degeneracy between primordial modulation and anisotropic galaxy bias, which is substantially broken by adding peculiar-velocity information: the density-velocity cross-spectrum complements the galaxy auto-spectrum while the velocity auto-spectrum constrains the primordial modulation independently of anisotropic bias. Velocity information becomes increasingly effective for more negative scale dependence, yielding constraints tighter than BOSS for k^{-1} and k^{-2} modulations.
AI.conclusion: Peculiar-velocity information provides a complementary avenue for testing primordial power asymmetry with large-scale structure, particularly valuable for quadrupolar asymmetry in the presence of anisotropic galaxy bias, where it can break otherwise severe degeneracies and improve constraints beyond current surveys.

title: Cosmographic Reconstruction of the Quintessence Potential in Scalar-Tensor Gravity
comment: 25 pages, 5 figures. The numerical analysis files used for the reproduction of the figures can be found at: https://github.com/leandros11/st-reconstruction
summary: We generalise the cosmographic reconstruction programme of Chakraborty, Dunsby & Scherrer to scalar-tensor gravity. Working in the Jordan frame with a general non-minimal coupling $F(Φ)$, we derive exact closed-form expressions for the potential slope $λ_U$, the coupling slope $λ_F$, and their curvature parameters $Γ_U$ and $Γ_F$ in terms of the cosmographic parameters $(q,j,s)$, the Planck-mass running $α_M = d\ln F/d\ln a$ and its derivatives. We express $α_M$ and its derivatives in terms of a set of coefficients $g_n$ describing the time variation of the gravitational constant $G\propto F^{-1}$, casting all four quantities in fully observable form. We then evaluate the reconstruction against current data, including DESI~DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation measurements and Lunar Laser Ranging constraints on $\dot G/G$, propagating the cosmographic uncertainties through to the reconstructed potential. All expressions reduce analytically to those of Chakraborty, Dunsby & Scherrer in the minimally-coupled limit, which we verify symbolically. We find that the potential slope $λ_U$ is recovered at the few-tenths level while the curvature $Γ_U$ is essentially unconstrained. We further show that the positivity of the scalar kinetic term is equivalent to $w_{\rm eff,0}\ge-1$, so that the region of cosmographic parameter space closed to minimally-coupled quintessence is exactly the phantom region, and that the non-minimal coupling reopens it through a single coefficient $g_2$ of the gravitational tower. Because Lunar Laser Ranging forces $|g_1|\lesssim2\times10^{-4}$ while the reconstruction is sensitive to $g_2\sim O(0.1)$, the framework presupposes that $α_M$ is passing through zero at the present epoch, as expected on the Damour--Nordtvedt least-coupling attractor.

AI.tldr: The authors extend the cosmographic reconstruction programme to scalar-tensor gravity, deriving exact closed-form expressions for potential and coupling slopes and their curvature parameters in terms of cosmographic observables (q, j, s), the Planck-mass running α_M, and coefficients g_n encoding the time variation of G. They validate against DESI DR2 BAO and Lunar Laser Ranging data, recovering λ_U to few-tenths precision while leaving Γ_U unconstrained. They show the positivity of the scalar kinetic term maps to w_eff,0 ≥ -1, establishing that the phantom region is excluded for minimally-coupled quintessence but reopened by non-minimal coupling via the g_2 coefficient, while LLR bounds force α_M to pass through zero today as on the Damour–Nordtvedt attractor.
AI.motivation: To generalise the existing cosmographic reconstruction formalism (originally developed for minimally-coupled quintessence by Chakraborty, Dunsby & Scherrer) to scalar-tensor gravity with non-minimal coupling, thereby enabling model-independent reconstruction of the scalar potential and coupling from observational cosmographic parameters.
AI.method: Working in the Jordan frame with a general non-minimal coupling F(Φ), the authors derive exact closed-form expressions for λ_U, λ_F, Γ_U, and Γ_F in terms of cosmographic parameters (q, j, s), the Planck-mass running α_M, and its derivatives. These are recast in observable form via coefficients g_n describing the time variation of the gravitational constant G ∝ F^{-1}. The reconstruction is evaluated against DESI DR2 BAO and Lunar Laser Ranging constraints on Ġ/G, with uncertainties propagated through the reconstructed potential. Symbolic verification of the minimal-coupling limit is performed, and the kinetic-term positivity condition is analysed in terms of the effective equation-of-state parameter.
AI.result: The potential slope λ_U is recovered at the few-tenths level, while the curvature Γ_U remains essentially unconstrained by current data. The positivity of the scalar kinetic term is exactly equivalent to w_eff,0 ≥ -1, implying minimally-coupled quintessence is excluded in the phantom region of cosmographic parameter space. Non-minimal coupling reopens this region through the single coefficient g_2 of the gravitational tower. Lunar Laser Ranging imposes |g_1| ≲ 2×10^-4 while the reconstruction is sensitive to g_2 ~ O(0.1), which presupposes α_M passes through zero at the present epoch, consistent with the Damour–Nordtvedt least-coupling attractor.
AI.conclusion: The generalised cosmographic reconstruction provides a fully observable framework for scalar-tensor gravity, analytically reducing to the minimal-coupling limit. Current data constrain the potential slope but not its curvature. The analysis reveals a precise mapping between kinetic-term positivity and the phantom divide, and shows that observational constraints imply the system sits near the Damour–Nordtvedt least-coupling attractor, with α_M passing through zero today.

title: Cosmicflows-4 and the Cosmological Consistency of Large-Scale Motions
summary: We study coherent flows in Cosmicflows-4 (CF4) and its constituent catalogs. We fit monopole and dipole moments in nonoverlapping radial bins using a log-distance radial-velocity estimator. For each sample, the Planck 2018 $Λ$CDM prediction accounts for the actual positions, statistical weights, velocity covariance, and measurement covariance. Across six bins extending to $300,h^{-1},\mathrm{Mpc}$, the All Individual sample is broadly consistent with $Λ$CDM, with dipole and joint deviations of $2.29σ$ and $2.36σ$. The strongest localized feature occurs at $120$--$160,h^{-1},\mathrm{Mpc}$, where $|V_{\rm dip}|=628\pm82,\mathrm{km,s^{-1}}$ and the dipole deviation reaches $3.40σ$. The excess is concentrated toward negative supergalactic X and depends strongly on the survey window. TFR and 6dFGS favor larger dipoles, while SDSS and SN favor smaller ones. Removing 6dFGS reduces the upper-bin dipole deviation to $1.56σ$, while removing SN raises it to $3.77σ$. Nevertheless, the SN and 6dFGS dipoles remain mutually consistent when their covariance is included. SDSS is consistent with $Λ$CDM through $160,h^{-1},\mathrm{Mpc}$ but shows a separate rise at larger radii whose significance depends on the treatment of the monopole and shared distance-scale covariance. Overall, CF4 does not show uniformly anomalous motion across its full radial range. Instead, it contains localized and window-dependent features that should be tested with selection-matched mock catalogs and correlated calibration uncertainties.

AI.tldr: This paper studies peculiar velocities in the Cosmicflows-4 catalog, fitting monopole and dipole moments in radial bins out to 300 h⁻¹ Mpc. The data are broadly consistent with ΛCDM overall (2.29σ dipole deviation), but a localized 3.40σ excess dipole is found at 120–160 h⁻¹ Mpc. The significance is highly survey-window dependent: removing 6dFGS drops the upper-bin deviation to 1.56σ, while removing SN increases it to 3.77σ.
AI.motivation: To test whether the peculiar velocity field in Cosmicflows-4 reveals coherent bulk flows or other anomalies that challenge the standard ΛCDM model, and to understand how these measurements depend on survey windows and calibration assumptions.
AI.method: Fits monopole and dipole velocity moments in six nonoverlapping radial bins to 300 h⁻¹ Mpc using a log-distance radial-velocity estimator. Each sample is compared against Planck 2018 ΛCDM predictions that account for actual galaxy positions, statistical weights, velocity covariance, and measurement covariance, with tests on constituent catalogs (TFR, 6dFGS, SDSS, SN) and window-removal experiments.
AI.result: CF4 is broadly consistent with ΛCDM (dipole deviation 2.29σ, joint 2.36σ). A localized 3.40σ dipole excess of 628±82 km/s appears at 120–160 h⁻¹ Mpc, concentrated toward negative supergalactic X. TFR and 6dFGS favor larger dipoles; SDSS and SN favor smaller ones. Removing 6dFGS reduces the upper-bin deviation to 1.56σ; removing SN raises it to 3.77σ. SDSS is consistent with ΛCDM through 160 h⁻¹ Mpc but shows a separate rise at larger radii.
AI.conclusion: CF4 does not display uniformly anomalous bulk motion across its full radial range. Instead, it contains localized, window-dependent features whose significance varies with subsample. These features should be tested with selection-matched mock catalogs and correlated calibration uncertainty treatments before claiming any deviation from ΛCDM.

title: How X-rays heat the IGM in different 21-cm simulation codes: a comparison between Licorice and Beorn
summary: Any interpretation of the 21-cm signal of neutral hydrogen using Bayesian inference methods can only be as accurate as the underlying simulation code used to model the state of the intergalactic medium (IGM). 3D radiative transfer (RT) simulation codes may capture complex physics, but are computationally expensive and, therefore, faster, more approximate codes have been developed. To improve our understanding of the convergence of simulation codes in the 21-cm science community, we present a comparison of the X-ray heating of the IGM modelled in Licorice, a 3D RT simulation code, and Beorn, a 1D RT code. We use Beorn to process sources extracted from Licorice simulations, using the same physics of the sources, in order to obtain two versions of the temperature of the IGM heated by X-rays. We observe a good agreement between the luminosity fields, mean temperatures, and global 21-cm signal of the two setups, but discrepancies in the distribution of temperature and 21-cm signal, which result in a $\sim 30\%$ difference in the 21-cm power spectrum. We attempt to isolate the approximations that lead to these differences and find that common approximations used in 1D RT codes produce effects of that magnitude. Using an emulator of the Licorice power spectra in an MCMC pipeline, we translate these differences between power spectra into differences between posterior distributions over the astrophysical parameters. We observe a typical bias between 1D posteriors of $\gtrsim 1 σ$ (with a noise level corresponding to 100h of SKA observations).

AI.tldr: A comparison between Licorice (3D radiative transfer) and Beorn (1D radiative transfer) codes for modeling X-ray heating of the IGM shows good agreement in global quantities but ~30% differences in the 21-cm power spectrum, leading to >1σ biases in astrophysical parameter posteriors.
AI.motivation: Bayesian inference of the 21-cm signal depends critically on the accuracy of underlying simulation codes. Since 3D RT codes are computationally prohibitive, faster 1D approximations are widely used, making it essential to quantify the systematic errors introduced by these approximations and their impact on parameter inference.
AI.method: The authors run Licorice (3D RT) simulations and use Beorn (1D RT) to process the same sources extracted from Licorice with identical source physics, producing two versions of the X-ray-heated IGM temperature. They compare luminosity fields, mean temperatures, global 21-cm signal, temperature/21-cm distributions, and power spectra. They isolate which 1D approximations drive the discrepancies, then use an emulator of Licorice power spectra in an MCMC pipeline to translate power-spectrum differences into posterior biases.
AI.result: The two codes agree on luminosity fields, mean temperatures, and the global 21-cm signal, but differ in the temperature and 21-cm spatial distributions, yielding ~30% differences in the 21-cm power spectrum. Common 1D RT approximations account for discrepancies of this magnitude. MCMC-based emulation translates these differences into ~1σ or greater biases in posterior distributions over astrophysical parameters, assuming noise levels corresponding to 100 hours of SKA observations.
AI.conclusion: 1D RT codes introduce systematic errors in the 21-cm power spectrum and astrophysical parameter inference that are non-negligible at SKA-era sensitivity, highlighting the need for caution when interpreting 21-cm constraints obtained with approximate radiative transfer codes.

title: Orbital Migration of Interacting Stellar Mass Black Holes in Disks around Supermassive Black Holes. III. Mass Distribution of Hierarchical Mergers
summary: Active galactic nucleus (AGN) disks are a promising location for the formation of binary black holes (BBHs) that will merge on relatively short timescales and be detected by LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK). To compare the mass function (MF) of black holes (BHs) undergoing hierarchical mergers in AGN disks to the inferred MFs from LVK observations, we perform 360 simulations with an N-body code augmented to include an analytic model for migration torques and other gas forces. We focus on the region surrounding migration traps in AGN disks where migration torques cancel out and BHs converge. We find that regardless of changes in the initial MF and BBH merger criteria, frequent mergers deplete the number of BHs with masses $\lesssim 10$~$M_\odot$ and fill the upper mass gap with a roughly uniform distribution from 40--100~$M_\odot$, with a slight overabundance around ${\approx}70~M_\odot$ from resonant orbiters. We also find an average merger rate of $\sim 6$~Gpc$^{-3}$~yr$^{-1}$ for migration-trap-aided BBH mergers in our AGN disk model. $\sim 40\%$ of these mergers have uneven mass ratios and 16\% have a primary mass $\in[50-100]~M_\odot$. Therefore, AGN disks could easily be the source of BBH mergers observed by LVK that are difficult to produce through traditional stellar evolution channels. Our simulations also form a separate higher-mass intermediate mass black hole (IMBH) population $>200~M_\odot$ after $\sim 2$~Myr. Future gravitational wave detectors can use observations of this IMBH population to constrain models of AGN accretion disks.

AI.tldr: This paper uses 360 N-body simulations with analytic gas/migration torque models to study hierarchical binary black hole mergers in AGN disk migration traps. The simulations show that frequent mergers deplete BHs below ~10 M☉, fill the upper mass gap (40-100 M☉) roughly uniformly with a slight overabundance near 70 M☉, produce an average merger rate of ~6 Gpc⁻³ yr⁻¹, and form a separate IMBH population >200 M☉ after ~2 Myr. AGN disks could explain LVK-observed BBH mergers that are hard to produce via stellar evolution.
AI.motivation: To determine whether AGN disks can produce binary black hole mergers consistent with LVK observations, particularly for mergers with masses and mass ratios that are difficult to explain through traditional stellar evolution channels.
AI.method: The authors perform 360 N-body simulations of black holes in AGN disks, augmented with an analytic model for migration torques and other gas forces, focusing on the migration trap region where torques cancel and BHs converge. They vary the initial mass function and BBH merger criteria to study the resulting merger mass function.
AI.result: Frequent mergers deplete low-mass BHs (≲10 M☉) and fill the upper mass gap (40-100 M☉) with a roughly uniform distribution, with slight overabundance near ~70 M☉ from resonant orbiters. The average merger rate is ~6 Gpc⁻³ yr⁻¹, ~40% of mergers have uneven mass ratios, and 16% have primary masses in [50-100] M☉. A separate IMBH population >200 M☉ forms after ~2 Myr.
AI.conclusion: AGN disks could be a dominant source of BBH mergers observed by LVK that are difficult to produce through stellar evolution. Future gravitational wave detectors can use the predicted IMBH population to constrain AGN disk models.

title: Abundant Heavy Black Hole Seeds from Moderate Lyman-Werner Radiation
summary: The existence of high-redshift quasars may indicate that massive black hole seeds formed via supermassive Population III stars in atomic-cooling halos with large gas inflow rates; however, the dependence of this process on halo assembly rate and radiative background remains poorly constrained. We present a large suite of 65 high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations of 15 pristine halos spanning a wide range of Lyman-Werner radiation backgrounds and halo assembly histories. We introduce a novel method to estimate the final Population III stellar mass from radial gas infall profiles at the onset of runaway collapse and validate it against simulations from the literature that explicitly follow protostellar accretion with sink particles, reproducing protostellar masses to within a factor of $\sim2$. We find a clear transition in gas inflow rates between halos exposed to $J_{\rm 21} \lesssim 1$ and $J_{\rm 21} \gtrsim 10$, with the latter frequently sustaining inflow rates above the adopted threshold for supermassive star formation and producing estimated stellar masses up to $10^{5} \, M_{\odot}$. In contrast, the halo assembly timescale, $M_{\rm Halo}$/$\dot{M}_{\rm Halo}$, shows no statistically significant correlation with predicted stellar mass, despite halo assembly rates spanning $0.01$-$7 \, M_{\rm \odot} \, {\rm yr}^{-1}$. The Lyman-Werner radiation field therefore is a stronger predictor of sustained high accretion within our parameter space. Finally, a semi-analytic model applied to cosmological volumes shows that halos exposed to intermediate Lyman-Werner backgrounds ($1 \lesssim J_{\rm 21} < 10$) are orders of magnitude more common than those in the high-$J_{\rm 21}$ tail. If sustained high accretion extends into this intermediate regime, heavy black hole seeds may form in substantially more common environments than required by classical direct-collapse scenarios.

AI.tldr: Using 65 high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations of 15 pristine halos, this paper investigates conditions for supermassive Population III star formation and massive black hole seed formation, finding that Lyman-Werner radiation background (not halo assembly rate) is the dominant predictor of sustained high gas inflow, and that intermediate LW backgrounds may allow heavy seed formation in more common environments than classical scenarios require.
AI.motivation: To constrain the dependence of massive black hole seed formation via supermassive Population III stars on halo assembly rate and radiative background, which remains poorly understood.
AI.method: A suite of 65 high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations of 15 pristine halos across a range of Lyman-Werner backgrounds and assembly histories. A novel method estimates final Population III stellar mass from radial gas infall profiles at runaway collapse onset, validated against sink-particle simulations to factor ~2 accuracy. A semi-analytic model is also applied to cosmological volumes.
AI.result: A clear transition in gas inflow rates exists between halos at J21 < 1 and J21 > 10, with the latter sustaining inflow rates above the supermassive star formation threshold and producing stellar masses up to 10^5 Msun. Halo assembly timescale shows no statistically significant correlation with predicted stellar mass. Intermediate LW backgrounds (1 < J21 < 10) are orders of magnitude more common than high-J21 environments.
AI.conclusion: The Lyman-Werner radiation field is a stronger predictor of sustained high accretion than halo assembly rate. If sustained high accretion extends into the intermediate J21 regime, massive black hole seeds may form in substantially more common environments than classical direct-collapse scenarios require.

title: Old Disks Die Hard: How Does AGN Feedback Suppress Disk Formation in Milky Way Mass Galaxies?
summary: The connection between a galaxy's visual shape and its star formation rate is one of the oldest established trends in galaxy evolution, yet the origin of this trend remains unsettled. We analyze two Milky-Way mass halos simulated with FIRE-2 galaxy formation physics, each run without AGN and with up to three implementations of AGN feedback. We use them to study how and why AGN star formation suppression affects morphological evolution over cosmic time. Both runs without AGN feedback produce prominent, thin, star-forming spiral disks at $z=0$. Each of the AGN runs has less late-time star formation, and ends up with a higher spheroid fraction and a lower thin-disk mass fraction. In two instances, the AGN runs produce quenched lenticular galaxies with no cool gas at $z=0$. The main reason for these morphological differences is that AGN feedback becomes effective {\em just after} the onset of disk formation, at ``spin up," in every run. This time-differentiated impact suppresses the formation of disk stars, especially thin-disk stars, preferentially because thin-disk formation occurs late. The spheroidal components are assembled early in all runs, before AGN feedback is effective, and are therefore similar in mass and size across runs.

AI.tldr: Using FIRE-2 simulations of Milky-Way mass halos with and without various AGN feedback implementations, the paper shows that AGN suppression of star formation just after disk formation ("spin up") preferentially reduces thin-disk star formation, leading runs with AGN to have higher spheroid fractions and lower thin-disk mass fractions, with some producing quenched lenticular galaxies.
AI.motivation: To understand the origin of the long-established trend between a galaxy's visual morphology and its star formation rate, specifically how AGN feedback suppresses star formation and affects morphological evolution over cosmic time.
AI.method: Analyze two Milky-Way mass halos simulated with FIRE-2 galaxy formation physics, each run without AGN and with up to three implementations of AGN feedback, comparing morphological evolution, spheroid fractions, thin-disk mass fractions, and star formation histories across runs.
AI.result: Runs without AGN produce prominent, thin, star-forming spiral disks at z=0. AGN runs have less late-time star formation, higher spheroid fractions, and lower thin-disk mass fractions; two AGN runs even produce quenched lenticular galaxies with no cool gas. The key mechanism is that AGN feedback becomes effective just after disk formation ("spin up"), preferentially suppressing late-forming thin-disk stars while leaving early-assembled spheroidal components largely unchanged.
AI.conclusion: The morphological difference between star-forming and quenched galaxies arises because AGN feedback becomes active just after disk formation begins, preferentially suppressing thin-disk star formation while spheroidal components, assembled earlier before AGN is effective, remain similar in mass and size across runs.

title: The CMZ Asymmetries: Feeding or Feedback?
summary: Three-fourths of the dense gas and dust in the CMZ is located at positive longitudes and positive radial velocities. The majority of compact 24 micrometer wavelength sources are at negative longitudes. These two asymmetries indicate either a recent asymmetric injection of gas along the bar dust lanes, or that most of the molecular gas is contained in a small number of massive, gravitationally bound clouds, or a major feedback episode which dissociated an entire sector of the CMZ's dense gas.

AI.tldr: The Galactic Center Molecular Zone (CMZ) shows significant spatial asymmetries: dense gas and dust concentrate at positive longitudes and radial velocities, while compact 24 μm sources dominate at negative longitudes. These asymmetries suggest either recent asymmetric gas injection along the bar's dust lanes, gas confined in a few massive bound clouds, or a major feedback event that dissociated a sector of the CMZ's dense gas.
AI.motivation: To identify and understand the physical mechanisms driving asymmetric distributions of dense gas and star formation in the Central Molecular Zone of the Milky Way.
AI.method: Comparative analysis of the spatial distributions of dense molecular gas/dust (via longitudes and radial velocities) versus compact 24 μm sources in the CMZ.
AI.result: Three-fourths of dense gas/dust resides at positive longitudes and positive radial velocities, while most compact 24 μm sources are at negative longitudes, revealing a clear spatial asymmetry between gas content and star-forming activity.
AI.conclusion: The observed asymmetries imply either asymmetric gas inflow along bar dust lanes, concentration of molecular gas into a few massive bound clouds, or a major feedback episode that dissociated dense gas in an entire sector of the CMZ.

title: Energy Partitioning in Dust-catalyzed $\mathrm{H_2}$ and HD Formation Revealed by Molecular Simulations Considering Nuclear Quantum Effects
summary: Molecular hydrogen formation on interstellar dust grains is a key surface process in the interstellar medium, but the redistribution of the recombination energy between the substrate and the nascent molecule remains poorly understood. Here, we use ring-polymer molecular dynamics (RPMD) with a machine-learning force field to investigate energy partitioning during $\mathrm{H_2}$ and $\mathrm{HD}$ formation on graphene at $T=25, 50$ and $100 \mathrm{K}$. We focus on the chemisorbed-H recombination pathway previously identified as the dominant low-temperature channel on bare graphitic surfaces when nuclear quantum effects are included. The desorbing molecule retains the major fraction of the effective surface-mediated released energy, while graphene absorbs a smaller but non-negligible part. This molecular retention fraction is nearly temperature-independent over the investigated range. In contrast, the post-formation molecular kinetic-energy distribution changes more strongly with temperature: rovibrational motion dominates at low temperature, whereas center-of-mass translation becomes increasingly important at $100 \mathrm{K}$. $\mathrm{H_2}$ and $\mathrm{HD}$ exhibit broadly similar total energy retention, with only modest isotope-dependent differences in their internal kinetic-energy partitioning. These results provide an energy-resolved microscopic picture of surface-mediated energy redistribution in $\mathrm{H_2}$/$\mathrm{HD}$ formation, with implications for formation-pumping signatures in high-excitation $\mathrm{H_2}$ lines, vibrationally excited $\mathrm{H_2}$ chemistry, and collisional excitation of coexisting molecules by translationally hot nascent $\mathrm{H_2}$ in cold interstellar gas.

AI.tldr: This paper uses ring-polymer molecular dynamics with a machine-learning force field to study energy partitioning during H2 and HD formation on graphene at 25, 50, and 100 K via the chemisorbed-H recombination pathway. The desorbing molecule retains most of the released energy while graphene absorbs a smaller but non-negligible fraction, with molecular retention being nearly temperature-independent. Temperature strongly affects the kinetic-energy distribution: rovibrational motion dominates at low T while translation grows at 100 K, with only modest isotope-dependent differences.
AI.motivation: The redistribution of recombination energy between the interstellar grain substrate and the nascent H2/HD molecule is poorly understood, yet it is critical for understanding formation-pumping signatures, vibrationally excited H2 chemistry, and collisional excitation of coexisting molecules in cold interstellar gas.
AI.method: Ring-polymer molecular dynamics (RPMD) simulations with a machine-learning force field, applied to H2 and HD formation on graphene via the chemisorbed-H recombination pathway at T = 25, 50, and 100 K. Nuclear quantum effects are included via the RPMD framework, and energy partitioning between the desorbing molecule and the graphene substrate is analyzed as a function of temperature and isotope.
AI.result: The desorbing molecule retains the majority of the surface-mediated released energy with near-temperature-independent retention fractions. Temperature strongly affects the post-formation kinetic-energy distribution: rovibrational energy dominates at low T, while center-of-mass translation becomes increasingly important at 100 K. H2 and HD show broadly similar total energy retention, with only modest isotope-dependent differences in internal kinetic-energy partitioning.
AI.conclusion: The work provides an energy-resolved microscopic picture of surface-mediated energy redistribution in H2/HD formation on interstellar dust grains, with implications for formation-pumping signatures in high-excitation H2 lines, vibrationally excited H2 chemistry, and collisional excitation of coexisting molecules by translationally hot nascent H2 in cold interstellar gas.

title: How mergers shape galaxy morphology in the IllustrisTNG simulation
summary: How galaxy mergers drive morphological evolution remains an open question. Traditional views hold that major mergers produce elliptical galaxies, while minor mergers form dispersion-dominated components such as galactic bulges. However, more recent work has challenged this simple picture, suggesting a more complex evolutionary scenario. In this study, we use the IllustrisTNG cosmological simulation to investigate how mergers shape galaxy morphology, across a broad range of galaxy masses and merger mass ratios. Our results show that the post-merger galaxy morphology is primarily determined by three factors: collision angle $\overlineθ$, cold gas fraction $f_\mathrm{cold\,gas}$, and pre-merger galaxy morphology $\mathrm{(B/T)_{*,pre}}$. Specifically, spiral-in mergers with large $\overlineθ$ increase the rotational support of the system, allowing the gas to settle into an extended disk. When the system is rich in cold gas, star formation within the newly formed gas disk can further strengthen the disk-dominated structure of the remnant. On the other hand, head-on mergers with small $\overlineθ$ typically disrupt ordered galactic motion, producing more dispersion-supported remnants. Overall, we interpret our results within a unified picture of merger-driven morphological transformation in galaxies.

AI.tldr: Using the IllustrisTNG cosmological simulation, the study shows that post-merger galaxy morphology is determined by collision angle, cold gas fraction, and pre-merger morphology—spiral-in, gas-rich mergers produce disk-dominated remnants, while head-on mergers produce dispersion-supported remnants.
AI.motivation: Traditional views hold that major mergers produce ellipticals and minor mergers produce bulges, but recent work challenges this simple picture. The authors aim to investigate how mergers drive morphological evolution across a broad range of galaxy masses and merger mass ratios to clarify the mechanism.
AI.method: The authors use the IllustrisTNG cosmological simulation to investigate how mergers shape galaxy morphology across a broad range of galaxy masses and merger mass ratios, examining the roles of collision angle, cold gas fraction, and pre-merger galaxy morphology.
AI.result: Post-merger morphology is primarily determined by three factors: collision angle, cold gas fraction, and pre-merger B/T ratio. Spiral-in mergers with large collision angles increase rotational support and, when gas-rich, allow extended disk formation with star formation reinforcing disk structure. Head-on mergers with small collision angles disrupt ordered motion, producing dispersion-supported remnants.
AI.conclusion: The authors propose a unified picture of merger-driven morphological transformation in galaxies, integrating collision geometry and gas content to explain how mergers can produce either disk-dominated or dispersion-dominated remnants.

title: The SAMI Galaxy Survey: Linking Tidal Features and Orbit Populations Using Schwarzschild Modelling
comment: 32 pages, 25 figures, accepted to Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society (MNRAS)
summary: The evolution of angular momentum in galaxies is shaped by a combination of internal secular processes and external mechanisms such as mergers. Orbit-superposition based dynamical modelling provides a powerful means of linking the intrinsic orbital structures of galaxies to their global properties and merger histories. We construct Schwarzschild orbit-superposition models of massive ($\log(M/M_{\odot})>10$) SAMI galaxies using the DYNAMITE code, utilising deep KiDS photometry to accurately reproduce each galaxy's luminosity distribution. We find that the fractions of hot, cold, warm, and counter-rotating orbits all show significant correlations with the spin parameter proxy $λ_{R_e}$, with the strongest correlation arising from the combined hot plus counter-rotating fraction. When controlling for stellar mass and environment, we find that the fraction of hot and cold orbits show significant correlations with stellar age, whereas warm orbits do not. We further find that the lower values of $λ_{R_e}$ for young galaxies with shell merger features as compared to the full sample is driven by an excess of hot orbits and a deficit of cold orbits, with no dependence on warm orbits. We suggest that the kinematic transformation in this SAMI sample proceeds through stars transitioning directly from cold to hot orbits. As warm orbits are expected to arise from secular heating processes, these findings indicate that merger-driven heating is the dominant mechanism governing the redistribution of angular momentum and the reduction of rotational support in massive galaxies.

AI.tldr: Using Schwarzschild orbit-superposition dynamical models of massive SAMI galaxies (built with DYNAMITE and KiDS photometry), the paper shows that hot and cold orbital fractions correlate with spin parameter λ_Re, while mergers (shell features) reduce rotation via an excess of hot orbits and deficit of cold orbits—with no change in warm orbits—indicating that merger-driven heating, not secular processes, dominates angular momentum redistribution.
AI.motivation: To understand what governs the transformation of angular momentum and rotational support in massive galaxies, and to determine whether mergers or secular internal processes dominate this kinematic evolution.
AI.method: Construct Schwarzschild orbit-superposition models of massive SAMI galaxies (log(M/M_sun)>10) using the DYNAMITE code, with deep KiDS photometry for accurate luminosity distributions. Quantify orbital fractions (hot, cold, warm, counter-rotating) and correlate them with spin parameter proxy λ_Re, stellar age, environment, and merger (shell) features, while controlling for stellar mass and environment.
AI.result: Hot, cold, warm, and counter-rotating orbital fractions all correlate significantly with λ_Re, strongest for combined hot plus counter-rotating fraction. After controlling for mass and environment, hot and cold fractions correlate with stellar age but warm orbits do not. Young galaxies with shell merger features show lower λ_Re driven by excess hot orbits and deficit cold orbits, with no warm-orbit dependence.
AI.conclusion: The kinematic transformation proceeds via stars transitioning directly from cold to hot orbits, bypassing warm orbits. Since warm orbits arise from secular heating, the results imply that merger-driven heating is the dominant mechanism redistributing angular momentum and reducing rotational support in massive galaxies.

title: The galaxies' energy balance problem solved
summary: We attempt to resolve the long-standing energy balance problem encountered by Radiative Transfer (RT) models, particularly in edge-on galaxies by incorporating a treatment for the clumpy structure of the Interstellar Medium (ISM). A subgrid approach is adopted, treating the quiescent dust clouds as pseudo-dust grains, with equivalent optical and thermal emission properties. Deriving key quantities such as the absorption, scattering and extinction cross-sections enables the virtualisation of the macroscopic clump into a microscopic pseudo-grain that can be included alongside the existing dust model constituents. The addition of the pseudo-grain results in a flatter extinction curve. A library of clump emission spectral energy distributions (SEDs) is constructed for radiation fields of various colours and intensities. The new clumpy model is applied to the edge-on galaxy NGC 891 and, for the first time, is able to achieve a good energy balance, simultaneously fitting both the submm and Near Infrared (NIR) data. The clumpy model is further applied to a small sample of seven galaxies of various inclinations, and the results are compared with those from the purely diffuse models. The clumpy models are characterised by a reduction in dust opacity, and therefore attenuation, compared to their purely diffuse counterparts. Thus, the maximum face-on optical depth in the $B$-band, ${\mathrm max}(τ^{\mathrm f}_{\mathrm B})$, derived from the clumpy models is found to be lower by factors ranging from 1.3 to 2.8. Of the seven galaxies, two are found to be optically thick in their centres, two are found to be moderately optically thick, and three are found to be optically thin.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the energy balance problem in edge-on galaxy Radiative Transfer models by introducing a subgrid treatment of clumpy ISM structure, treating dust clouds as pseudo-grains with equivalent optical/thermal properties. The clumpy model successfully achieves energy balance for NGC 891 and seven galaxies of varying inclinations, finding lower dust opacities and attenuations compared to purely diffuse models.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing energy balance problem encountered by Radiative Transfer (RT) models, particularly in edge-on galaxies, which stems from the simplified treatment of the ISM as a purely diffuse medium.
AI.method: A subgrid approach is adopted where quiescent dust clouds are treated as pseudo-dust grains with equivalent optical and thermal emission properties. Key cross-sections (absorption, scattering, extinction) are derived to virtualize macroscopic clumps into microscopic pseudo-grains included alongside existing dust model constituents. A library of clump emission SEDs is built for various radiation field colors and intensities, and the model is applied to edge-on galaxies.
AI.result: The clumpy model achieves good energy balance for NGC 891 for the first time, simultaneously fitting both submm and NIR data. Applied to seven galaxies, clumpy models show reduced dust opacity and attenuation compared to diffuse models, with maximum face-on B-band optical depth lower by factors of 1.3-2.8. Of the seven galaxies: two are optically thick in centers, two moderately optically thick, three optically thin.
AI.conclusion: The clumpy ISM treatment resolves the energy balance problem in RT models of edge-on galaxies and produces more accurate opacity estimates than purely diffuse models, with implications for how dust attenuation affects observed galaxy properties.

title: A Reproducible Two-Boundary Kinematic Correction for Baryonic Rotation-Curve Reconstruction in an 84-Galaxy SPARC Benchmark
summary: We present a reproducible computational validation and failure analysis of the empirical omega kinematic correction introduced by Flynn and Cannaliato (2025). The algorithm is deliberately minimal: one coefficient per galaxy is calculated from the innermost and outermost measured rotation-curve points and applied to the full observed radial profile before comparison with a baryonic reconstruction assembled from SPARC gas, disk, and bulge components. We preserve the predecessor's frozen 84-galaxy benchmark and publish its exact membership so that the transformation, not sample re-selection, is the object of validation. Without fitting the transformation to the baryonic residual, the primary maximum-disk reconstruction reduces the mean observed-baryonic discrepancy from 51.82 to 30.15 km/s across the frozen 84-galaxy benchmark. Bounded mass-to-light-ratio optimization further reduces the descriptive sensitivity-fit value to 25.45 km/s, while the simple Keplerian reference has a mean RMSE of 74.20 km/s in our earlier analysis [15]. Recalculation from the 84 per-galaxy records shows a resolved mass-to-light optimization benefit (delta RMSE > 0.05 km/s) in 53 galaxies and no resolved change in 31. Six galaxies do not beat the Keplerian reference; all six occur at Upsilon_max <= 0.111, whereas their omega values are not concentrated at the high end of the sample. We specify the complete deterministic workflow, native units, endpoint invariants, uncertainty propagation, and formula-level regression checks required to prevent grouping and sign errors. The complete 84-galaxy panel set, population-level error distributions, and failure diagnostics are retained as inspectable outputs. The result is a reproducible astronomical data-transformation benchmark rather than a proposed force law or replacement for dark matter or modified gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a reproducible computational validation and failure analysis of the omega kinematic correction introduced by Flynn and Cannaliato (2025), using a frozen 84-galaxy SPARC benchmark. The minimal algorithm (one coefficient per galaxy from innermost/outermost rotation-curve points) reduces mean observed-baryonic discrepancy from 51.82 to 30.15 km/s under maximum-disk reconstruction, and to 25.45 km/s with bounded mass-to-light optimization. Six galaxies fail to beat the Keplerian reference, all at Upsilon_max <= 0.111. The work provides a complete deterministic workflow and open benchmark, positioned as a data-transformation benchmark rather than a new force law.
AI.motivation: To provide a rigorous, reproducible validation of the empirical omega kinematic correction, ensuring that validation targets the transformation itself rather than sample re-selection, and to perform transparent failure analysis of the method.
AI.method: A deliberately minimal algorithm: one omega coefficient per galaxy computed from the innermost and outermost observed rotation-curve points, applied to the full observed radial profile before comparison with baryonic reconstructions from SPARC gas, disk, and bulge components. Bounded mass-to-light-ratio optimization is used, with the frozen 84-galaxy benchmark preserved and published exactly. Complete deterministic workflow, uncertainty propagation, and formula-level regression checks are specified.
AI.result: Maximum-disk reconstruction reduces mean observed-baryonic discrepancy from 51.82 to 30.15 km/s. Bounded mass-to-light optimization further reduces it to 25.45 km/s, versus the Keplerian reference RMSE of 74.20 km/s. 53 galaxies show resolved mass-to-light optimization benefit, 31 show no resolved change, and 6 fail to beat the Keplerian reference (all at Upsilon_max <= 0.111).
AI.conclusion: The omega correction is validated as a reproducible astronomical data-transformation benchmark with documented failure modes, but it is explicitly not proposed as a force law or replacement for dark matter or modified gravity.

title: The Galactic Centre G+0.633-0.0604 Molecular Cloud: A New Gold Mine for Astrochemistry
comment: 5 pages, 2 figures. Proceedings for the IAU Symposium 405 "Traversing the Galactic Center in Space and Time"
summary: Astrochemistry is living a golden age, with more than a quarter of the ~350 molecules in the current interstellar census having been detected over the last three years. One of the sources driving this progress is the G+0.693-0.027 cloud, located in the northern part of the Galactic Centre Sgr B2 complex. In this contribution, we present the astrochemical characterisation of G+0.633-0.0604, a newly discovered chemically rich molecular cloud at the southern edge of Sgr B2. With an inventory of >120 species, G+0.633 provides robust second detections of several prebiotic molecules only reported towards G+0.693, establishing it as the first confirmed astrochemical twin of G+0.693 while demonstrating that the extraordinary chemistry of this cloud is not unique. Furthermore, G+0.633 offers an observational advantage over G+0.693 since it displays half narrower linewidths. Together, G+0.633 and G+0.693 form a unique benchmark pair for unveiling molecular complexity and prebiotic chemistry in the interstellar medium.

AI.tldr: The paper presents the astrochemical characterization of G+0.633-0.0604, a newly discovered chemically rich molecular cloud at the southern edge of Sgr B2. With >120 detected species, it serves as the first confirmed astrochemical twin of G+0.693-0.027, providing second detections of several prebiotic molecules, while offering an observational advantage of half-narrower linewidths. Together they form a benchmark pair for studying molecular complexity and prebiotic chemistry in the interstellar medium.
AI.motivation: Astrochemistry is experiencing a golden age with rapid molecule discoveries, largely driven by the chemically rich cloud G+0.693-0.027. The authors aim to determine whether the extraordinary chemistry of G+0.693 is unique by searching for and characterizing analogous chemically rich sources, which could validate and expand the study of prebiotic chemistry in the interstellar medium.
AI.method: The authors perform a detailed astrochemical characterization of the newly discovered molecular cloud G+0.633-0.0604, located at the southern edge of Sgr B2. This involves establishing a full molecular inventory (>120 species) and comparing the chemical composition with that of G+0.693, including second detections of prebiotic molecules, along with analysis of linewidth properties for observational comparison.
AI.result: G+0.633 is confirmed as the first astrochemical twin of G+0.693, hosting >120 molecular species and providing robust second detections of several prebiotic molecules previously only reported toward G+0.693. It also demonstrates half narrower linewidths, offering an observational advantage over its twin.
AI.conclusion: The discovery establishes that the extraordinary chemistry observed in G+0.693 is not unique, and together G+0.633 and G+0.693 constitute a unique benchmark pair for advancing the study of molecular complexity and prebiotic chemistry in the interstellar medium.

title: OH Line Detections in Southern Galaxies of the IRAS Revised Bright Galaxy Sample
summary: We present a systematic study of OH main-line emission and absorption in 186 southern galaxies from the IRAS Revised Bright Galaxy Sample, using archival MeerKAT snapshot data. OH features are detected in 38 galaxies, including eight with OH maser emission (three new) and 30 showing OH absorption, mostly unreported previously. Four absorption systems exhibit weak OH emission superposed on strong absorption. OH-emitting regions are generally more compact than the associated radio continuum. Most absorption profiles are well fit by two Gaussian components (1667 and 1665 MHz), with an average integrated line ratio of $\sim$1.5. LIRGs show an OH emission detection rate of ~13\%, versus significantly lower rates in non-LIRGs. For sources with radio continuum flux densities >20 mJy, OH absorption detection rates reach ~36\% (LIRGs) and ~27\% (non-LIRGs), while no OH absorption features were detected among sources with lower radio continuum flux densities. This suggests that sufficient background continuum is likely an important factor for the detection of OH absorption. Detected OH emitters follow the empirical $L_{\rm OH}$--$L_{\rm FIR}$ relation, consistent with far-infrared pumping, while non-detections show upper limits below the relation. No significant differences are found between OH absorbers and non-detections in infrared luminosity or radio continuum compactness. Stacked spectra of non-detections reveal no significant OH features, suggesting that sensitivity and orientation alone do not fully explain the absence of absorption. In contrast, mid-infrared colors (e.g., W2--W3) and q_TIR differ between the two populations. OH absorption galaxies occupy an intermediate regime in L_HCN/L_CO between OH megamasers and non-detections, implying that OH absorption detectability is linked to dense molecular gas conditions, with extreme star formation potentially suppressing its occurrence.

AI.tldr: A systematic MeerKAT study of OH main-line emission and absorption in 186 southern galaxies from the IRAS Revised Bright Galaxy Sample, detecting OH features in 38 galaxies (8 maser emitters, 30 absorbers). Emission is linked to far-infrared pumping and dense molecular gas conditions, while absorption detection depends on sufficient background radio continuum.
AI.motivation: To systematically characterize OH main-line (1665/1667 MHz) emission and absorption across a large, well-defined sample of southern galaxies, and to understand the physical conditions governing OH detection—particularly the roles of far-infrared pumping, background continuum, and dense gas content.
AI.method: Used archival MeerKAT snapshot observations of 186 southern galaxies from the IRAS Revised Bright Galaxy Sample. Analyzed OH main-line spectra, separated emission and absorption components, fitted Gaussian profiles, compared detection rates across luminosity classes (LIRGs vs non-LIRGs) and radio continuum flux densities, correlated with infrared colors, q_TIR, and HCN/CO luminosity ratios, and produced stacked spectra of non-detections.
AI.result: OH features detected in 38 galaxies: 8 OH maser emitters (3 new) and 30 absorbers (mostly new). LIRGs have ~13% OH emission rate vs lower in non-LIRGs. OH absorption detected in ~36% (LIRGs) and ~27% (non-LIRGs) of sources with radio continuum >20 mJy, with no detections below this threshold. OH emitters follow the L_OH-L_FIR relation supporting far-infrared pumping. Stacked spectra of non-detections show no OH features. OH absorbers differ from non-detections in W2-W3 colors and q_TIR, and occupy an intermediate L_HCN/L_CO regime between megamasers and non-detections.
AI.conclusion: OH emission is governed by far-infrared pumping, while OH absorption requires sufficient background radio continuum, yet sensitivity and orientation alone cannot explain the absence of absorption. Mid-infrared colors, q_TIR, and dense-gas conditions (L_HCN/L_CO) distinguish absorbers from non-detections, suggesting that extreme star formation may suppress OH absorption detectability.

title: The deepest color-magnitude diagrams for the benchmark open cluster NGC 2437 from Gaia and VVVX
comment: 9 pages, 12 figures, 1 tables. Accepted for Publication in A&A
summary: Deep photometry of Galactic star clusters provides one of the most powerful tools for determining their physical properties. In particular, in low Galactic latitude regions that suffer from heavy extinction and crowding. NGC2437 is the most extended star cluster in the near-IR footprint of the VVV Extended Survey (VVVX), covering more than one degree on the sky. We aim to characterize its physical properties using Gaia DR3 in the optical and the VVVX in the near-IR. We use Gaia DR3 proper motions to select NGC2437 members in order to make optical and near-IR color-magnitude and color-color diagrams. We further exploited the newly constructed VVVX deep stack images to obtain the deepest near-IR color-magnitude diagram currently available for this cluster. We estimate the main physical parameters for NGC2437, including the mean parallax of 0.608 mas and PMs (-3.85, 0.41) mas/yr. The mean reddening E(J-Ks) = 0.059 mag and extinction of A_k = 0.034 mag for the cluster field, with no significant differential reddening spread. A distance modulus of 11.08 mag is estimated, equivalent to a distance of 1644 pc. This places NGC2437 at z=115 pc above the Galactic plane and at a galactocentric distance of 9.24 kpc. We measure the cluster structural parameters, obtaining a core radius of 10.79 arcmin. The estimated total absolute magnitudes are Mk = -4.91 mag and Mv = -3.70 mag. The cluster mean age is 350 Myr, using PARSEC-COLIBRI isochrones for solar metallicity. We measure a binary fraction of 28.6%. We also discuss the implications of the revised cluster parameters for the nearby open cluster NGC2425, the planetary nebula NGC2438, and the evolved OH/IR source OH231.8+04.2. The VVVX deep stacks increase the Ks photometric depth by 1.6 mag, nearly doubling the detected point sources and enabling significantly improved studies of stellar populations throughout the southern Galactic plane.

AI.tldr: The paper characterizes NGC2437, a large Galactic open cluster, using Gaia DR3 (optical) and VVVX (near-IR) data, determining its distance (1644 pc), age (350 Myr), reddening, structural parameters, and binary fraction, and discusses implications for nearby objects.
AI.motivation: Deep photometry of Galactic star clusters is a powerful tool for determining physical properties, especially in low Galactic latitude regions suffering from heavy extinction and crowding. NGC2437 is the most extended star cluster in the VVVX footprint, and characterizing it requires combining optical and near-IR data.
AI.method: Gaia DR3 proper motions were used to select NGC2437 members for optical and near-IR color-magnitude and color-color diagrams. Newly constructed VVVX deep stack images were exploited to obtain the deepest near-IR CMD currently available for this cluster.
AI.result: Mean parallax 0.608 mas; PMs (-3.85, 0.41) mas/yr; reddening E(J-Ks)=0.059 mag; extinction Ak=0.034 mag; distance modulus 11.08 mag (1644 pc); z=115 pc; galactocentric distance 9.24 kpc; core radius 10.79 arcmin; Mk=-4.91 mag, Mv=-3.70 mag; age 350 Myr; binary fraction 28.6%. VVVX deep stacks increase Ks depth by 1.6 mag, nearly doubling detected point sources.
AI.conclusion: The revised cluster parameters have implications for nearby NGC2425, the planetary nebula NGC2438, and the OH/IR source OH231.8+04.2, and demonstrate the value of VVVX deep stacks for improved stellar population studies in the southern Galactic plane.

title: ATLAS. IV. A JWST+MUSE Demographic Study of Ly$α$ Profiles in Little Red Dots
summary: We present an initial demographic study of Ly$α$ profiles in little red dots (LRDs) at $z=3$--9 using $R\sim1000$--4000 spectroscopy. Our sample consists of 8 LRDs observed in the VLT/MUSE Deep and Wide surveys and 23 LRDs observed with JWST/NIRSpec grating spectroscopy from JADES, CANUCS, and GO programs including SPURS. We identify Ly$α$ emission in 5 MUSE LRDs and 9 JWST LRDs. Only two of them exhibit broad Ly$α$ emission (FWHM $>1000\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$), both reported previously. The other Ly$α$-emitting LRDs show narrow Ly$α$ emission (FWHM $<1000\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$), with FWHMs mostly in the range 300--600 $\mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, comparable to or slightly larger than those of high-redshift star-forming galaxies (100--500 $\mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$). We measure the fraction of broad Ly$α$ emitters above a broad Ly$α$ luminosity threshold of $L_{\mathrm{Ly}α,\mathrm{broad}}=10^{42}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, obtaining $0.10^{+0.12}_{-0.07}$ for LRDs, about five times higher than the $2σ$ upper limit of $<0.02$ for high-redshift star-forming galaxies. Although we reproduce the broad Ly$α$ component reported in a previous stacking analysis of eight LRDs, albeit with a large uncertainty, we find no evidence for broad Ly$α$ emission in either the larger JWST stack, after excluding the two individually detected broad Ly$α$ emitters, or the higher-resolution MUSE stack. These results suggest that broad Ly$α$ emission is not ubiquitous among LRDs. Instead, LRDs with broad Ly$α$ emission appear to represent a rare population that may correspond to a particular evolutionary stage, potentially associated with unusually strong outflows or other distinctive physical conditions.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a demographic study of Lyα emission profiles in 31 little red dots (LRDs) at z=3-9 using VLT/MUSE and JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy. While 14 LRDs show Lyα emission, only 2 exhibit broad Lyα (FWHM >1000 km/s), both previously known. The broad Lyα fraction among LRDs (~0.10) is about five times higher than in star-forming galaxies (<0.02), but stacking analyses show no ubiquitous broad Lyα component, suggesting broad Lyα emitters represent a rare evolutionary phase possibly tied to strong outflows.
AI.motivation: To characterize the Lyα emission properties of little red dots (LRDs)—a population of compact, red, high-redshift galaxies—and to determine whether broad Lyα emission is a common or rare feature, which bears on understanding their physical nature and evolutionary state.
AI.method: Using R~1000-4000 spectroscopy from VLT/MUSE Deep and Wide surveys (8 LRDs) and JWST/NIRSpec from JADES, CANUCS, and GO programs including SPURS (23 LRDs), the authors measured Lyα emission profiles, classified them as broad (FWHM >1000 km/s) or narrow (FWHM <1000 km/s), and performed stacking analyses to search for broad Lyα components in larger samples.
AI.result: Lyα emission detected in 14 out of 31 LRDs (5 MUSE, 9 JWST). Only 2 show broad Lyα, both previously reported. The remaining emitters have narrow Lyα with FWHM mostly 300-600 km/s. The broad Lyα fraction above 10^42 erg/s is 0.10^{+0.12}_{-0.07} for LRDs, ~5x higher than the <0.02 upper limit for star-forming galaxies. Stacking reproduces the previously reported broad component only in the small 8-LRD stack, not in larger JWST or MUSE stacks after excluding the two broad emitters.
AI.conclusion: Broad Lyα emission is not ubiquitous among LRDs; it represents a rare population, possibly corresponding to a specific evolutionary stage characterized by strong outflows or distinctive physical conditions. This refines the picture of LRDs beyond earlier stacking-based claims of universal broad Lyα emission.
